newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Farmer sales remain slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Farmer sales remain slow.

text.p: Bids for dark northern spring were mostly lower on Friday amid slow farm sales as farmers focused on seeding in many parts of the Northern Plains.
Farmers were targeting $4.70 on 13 percent winter wheat. But there was not much old crop spring wheat left, a Montana merchandiser said.
"Farmers were expected to get into the fields by Monday if the weather holds," the dealer said. "Right now you cannot get into the fields because it is too muddy."
Another Montana dealer said farmers were seeding all the way from Wolfpoint to Cutbank, Montana.
"They are planting in between the rain showers. We are 20 days behind and for every day it rains, it takes three days to get the crop in," he said.
MGE spring wheat settled 2-1/2 to 7-3/4 cents lower with July down 6-1/2 cents at $4.35 a bushel.
